We moved to the apartment we are at now a year ago. We used to live with her sister and another couple. We’ll call my girlfriend L and her sister J. We moved because J would always have people over , and we wanted the privacy of no roommates. Once we moved, someone took our spot there. Fast forward from when we left (May 2018) to January 1st, 2020. J fucked her roommates over by not paying the rent for two months, as our landlords just accepted cash. For two months, she took the $3000 spent it on “bills” that her sister isn’t even sure about. After ruining her relationship with her roommates, She got the money from family to pay the rent off, and asked L and I to move in until the end of January. Her uncle would pick her up and she’d move out of state. She basically never asked the uncle to come get her, mentioned to L that she might just stay in New York. My girlfriend, who isn’t confrontational, never opposed her living with us for free. So J has been with us for about 4 months, no job, just contributing sometimes with cooking. She only comes here to sleep after she parties with her friends. Our house is essentially a hangover den. What makes matters worse is because of the current situation, the job she had a chance at has shut down. So shes not even looking for work. But that isn’t stopping her from going out every other night, to parties, where she doesn’t even think that if she was to get sick from being stupid, it would affect us as well. L wants her out, but is really conflicted because it’s her sister. I don’t think she’d be happy about me speaking to J about it, even though she also wants J out. I don’t want to seem like a dick, but it’s at the point where I might just take the risk of L being mad at me. I want my home back. I’ve been trying to get L to talk to her, but she just hates confrontation. I think I might just have to tell J if she doesn’t find a job to fund her getting her own place, she needs to to back to her mothers. WIBTA?

In essence, the key to maintaining independent thought within a community lies in fostering an environment that values diverse perspectives and encourages personal reflection.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to kick my girlfriend's older sister out of our apartment. Let me start by understanding the situation better. We've been living together for two years, and we moved to our current apartment a year ago. We moved because her sister, J, was always having people over, and we wanted more privacy without roommates. That worked out well for a while, but now J is back in our lives, and it's causing a lot of stress. From what I gather, J has been staying with us for about four months. She doesn't have a job, and she only contributes sometimes with cooking. She comes home to sleep after partying with her friends, and our house has become a hangover den. That's not ideal, especially since we're trying to maintain a stable home environment. What's worse is that because of the current situation, the job J had a chance at has shut down, so she's not even looking for work. But that doesn't stop her from going out every other night to parties. She doesn't seem to care about the potential health risks, like getting sick from being out and about, which could affect all of us. My girlfriend, L, doesn't want to confront her sister, which is making things harder. I want J out, but I'm really conflicted because it's her sister. I don't think L would be happy if I spoke to J about it, even though L also wants J out. I don't want to seem like a jerk, but it's at the point where I might just take the risk of L being mad at me. I want my home back. I've been trying to get L to talk to her, but she just hates confrontation. I think I might just have to tell J that if she doesn't find a job to fund her getting her own place, she needs to go back to her mother's. So, is it right or wrong for me to kick J out? I need to think about this carefully. On one hand, J's behavior is affecting our living situation, and we deserve a peaceful home. On the other hand, J is family, and kicking her out might strain our relationships further. I should consider the impact on everyone involved. If I kick J out, how will that affect L? She might be upset with me for confronting her sister. But if J stays, our home will continue to be disrupted, and it might lead to more tension between us. I also need to think about J's situation. She's not working and seems to be irresponsible with her actions. Is there a way to help her get back on her feet without sacrificing our own peace of mind? Maybe setting some boundaries or conditions for her staying with us could work. But if J isn't willing to change her behavior or find a job, then maybe it's necessary to ask her to leave. It's tough, but our home should be a safe and comfortable place for both of us. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Could we find a way for J to contribute more, like helping with bills or chores, in exchange for staying? Or maybe she could find temporary housing elsewhere while she gets her life together. However, if J isn't willing to take responsibility for her actions and continues to disrupt our home, then it might be the right decision to ask her to leave. It's important to stand up for our own well-being and the stability of our relationship with L. In the end, I think it's a tough call, but if J's behavior is negatively impacting our home and relationship, then it might be necessary to take action, even if it means confronting her and potentially upsetting L.
